lean_scaffold:
-- IGProtocol scaffold: VINIT → TANCH → FSPLIT → AFWD → AREV → EVALT → EVALF → ENGAGR → CLINK → IMSCRIB → IFIX → FFUSE → TANCH
-- (native ob3ect designer; elaborate against the kernel to verify)
name: The seam: the two-glyph join ⊣⊢ where one IMASM

phase_0.boundary_condition: The outer TANCH (⊢) and VINIT (⊣) that enclose the entire concatenated word, beyond which no further program joins occur.
phase_0.domain_name: The seam: the two-glyph join ⊣⊢ where one IMASM
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: The directed edge from TANCH to VINIT across the seam.
AFWD.justification: It represents the forward morphism of program concatenation, carrying the composition from one program to the next.

AREV.chosen_element: The in-edge received by VINIT from the preceding TANCH.
AREV.justification: It is the contravariant descent into the new program, the reverse of the forward join, which violates VINIT's source status.

CLINK.chosen_element: The sequential chaining of programs via seams.
CLINK.justification: It composes the eleven internal seams into a single linear word, linking each program's output to the next's input.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The Belnap B verdict on the seamless 115-glyph form.
ENGAGR.justification: It holds both the transformation closure and the paradox simultaneously, neither resolving to T nor F.

EVALF.chosen_element: The paradox-held verdict (B) produced by check on the 115-glyph seamless form.
EVALF.justification: The negative branch where ENGAGR engages a paradox, holding both closure and contradiction without resolution.

EVALT.chosen_element: The ill-typed verdict (F) produced by check on the 137-glyph form.
EVALT.justification: The affirmative branch where the seam's in-edge to VINIT is detected as a violation, yielding a negative type-check result.

FFUSE.chosen_element: The reconstitution of the full word from its two program halves.
FFUSE.justification: It fuses the two programs back into the original concatenated word, preserving the total glyph count and structure.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The seam ⊣⊢ itself, splitting the concatenated word into two programs.
FSPLIT.justification: It branches the single word into two distinct program paths: the preceding program and the following program.

IFIX.chosen_element: The IFIX at position 4 in the weight tool's linear read.
IFIX.justification: It permanently fixes the register, rendering all subsequent steps inert, mirroring the VINIT in-degree violation as a linear wall.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: The self-referential structure of the wordbook entry as a whole.
IMSCRIB.justification: The entry is itself a sequence of programs, each defined in terms of the same twelve-type grammar, making it self-identical under the IMASM framework.

TANCH.chosen_element: The closing glyph of each program before a seam.
TANCH.justification: It anchors the boundary of one program, emitting an out-edge across the seam to the next program's VINIT.

VINIT.chosen_element: The first glyph of a new program in the wordbook entry, immediately following a seam.
VINIT.justification: It is the uninitialized source of a fresh program, receiving an in-edge from the preceding TANCH via the seam, violating its arity_in=0.

phase_3.both_description: The state where the seam simultaneously carries a verdict (F or B) and contributes nothing to topology, closure, or phase structure.
phase_3.false_description: The paradox-held verdict B, where ENGAGR engages a contradiction that is sound to hold but not clean to resolve.
phase_3.true_description: The ill-typed verdict F, where the seam's edge into VINIT is detected as a structural violation.
phase_3.void_description: The state before any program in the wordbook entry is emitted, where no glyphs exist and no seams have formed.

steps.domain_action: first program begins, uninitialized and source-less
first program closes, anchoring its boundary
seam ⊣⊢ splits the word into two program paths
forward morphism carries composition across the seam to the next program
in-edge descends into the next program's VINIT, violating its arity_in=0
check detects the VINIT in-degree violation, yielding verdict F (ill-typed)
seamless form holds the paradox, yielding verdict B (paradox held)
Belnap B engages both closure and contradiction without resolution
eleven seams chain sequentially into a single linear word
the wordbook entry is itself a sequence of twelve programs under IMASM
position 4 fixes the register, rendering all later steps inert in linear read
rejoined word reconstitutes the original concatenated twelve programs
final program closes, sealing the entire word

phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical reference is the 137-glyph word for fibonacci_anyon_qc, with its eleven seams and twelve programs.
phase_5.compiler_frontend: The IMASM wordbook emitter that renders each catalog entry as twelve concatenated programs.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The seam ⊣⊢ serves as the inter-program communication channel, passing edges between TANCH and VINIT.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The glyph sequence itself, stored as a linear string of 137 or 115 characters, with seams marking program boundaries.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The cycle tool, which rotates the ring to census all cuts and reveal the six phase landings.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One VINIT in-degree violation per seam, eleven total, each consuming a structural check cycle.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the seam decides the verdict but contributes nothing to the network's vertices, edges, branches, merges, or μ∘δ closure, making the cycle entropy-conservative.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A verdict of F (ill-typed) on the 137-glyph form, or B (paradox held) on the 115-glyph seamless form, with topology, closure, and phase structure unchanged.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A concatenated word of twelve programs joined by eleven seams, each seam carrying an edge from TANCH to VINIT.
